long_biography.plain_text:
Fondazione MAIRE turned Fabrizio Di Amato's industrial experience towards education for the energy transition. As founder and chairman, he supports training that combines technical engineering with critical, social and humanistic skills. The foundation also preserves the group's historical engineering archive, placing industrial memory alongside study of future technologies.

Its programmes introduce secondary-school and university students to hydrogen, circular chemistry and sustainable industrial processes. A "humanist engineer" model treats technical competence and broad judgement as complementary, while the Climate Goals research programme examines skills needed for decarbonisation across different countries. Students and researchers can also consult digitised plans and documents from more than a century of engineering work.
